headline: High-risk shared-workspace interaction: Cline can write/egress broadly while OpenBBTerminal consumes MCP/REST inputs, creating leakage, conflict, and cascading-error paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files and use MCP, while OpenBBTerminal can consume MCP/REST inputs and stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if Cline writes attacker-controlled content into shared files or MCP payloads that OpenBBTerminal treats as data. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are connected through the same workspace or MCP server
IF OpenBBTerminal parses Cline-produced file or MCP content as trusted input
mitigations: Disable shared MCP endpoints between the agents
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Add a manual review step before OpenBBTerminal consumes Cline outputs
Prefix all inter-agent files with provenance metadata
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization and schema validation on shared inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and has broad network egress; OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data and exposes REST/MCP interfaces. If they share a workspace, Cline can read sensitive files and potentially transmit them outward, while OpenBBTerminal may ingest or expose those same files. The shared-file path is enough for medium severity.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem workspace
IF Cline is allowed to read files containing financial or licensed data
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Restrict Cline network egress to approved domains
Keep financial datasets out of the shared workspace
Rotate any exposed API keys or secrets after shared use
requires-engineering: add per-agent access controls on workspace files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has unrestricted filesystem write and git modification in a per-workspace session, while OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and localhost services but has no filesystem write. Direct write-write conflict is limited, yet both can mutate shared workspace artifacts through the filesystem or connected services, so concurrent interference is plausible. Uncertainty favors medium over low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or workspace
IF OpenBBTerminal writes artifacts through an MCP-connected service or localhost endpoint
mitigations: Run the agents in separate repositories
Pause one agent while the other edits shared files
Use git locks or branch-per-agent workflows
Avoid letting OpenBBTerminal write into Cline-managed workspaces
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived facts, and file edits; OpenBBTerminal can consume APIs and MCP inputs. If OpenBBTerminal treats Cline output as authoritative, errors can cascade into financial analysis or downstream actions. There is no evidence of built-in verification between them, so the default interaction is risky but not clearly high-impact irreversible.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal ingests Cline-produced files or MCP messages without verification
IF downstream outputs from OpenBBTerminal are used for decisions or reports
mitigations: Require source citations before OpenBBTerminal accepts Cline outputs
Add a human review gate for any financial recommendation
Compare outputs against an independent data source
Limit Cline to drafting, not final analysis
requires-engineering: implement provenance and confidence checks between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles source code and browser screenshots, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial and licensed data. If EU PII, licensed datasets, or regulated financial records flow through the pair, mismatched retention or residency controls can create compliance gaps. The profiles do not document aligned controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial data or licensed data is processed in the shared workflow
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the two agents
mitigations: Keep regulated datasets out of the pair unless approved
Document retention rules for each agent
Delete shared artifacts after each session
Confirm data-processing agreements for any external services
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies across both tools
